hints: Look at the left-hand end of each diagram and read off the instantaneous displacement of each of the three equal-amplitude waves.
Recall that the resultant displacement at any instant is the vector sum $y = y_1 + y_2 + y_3$ by the principle of superposition.
Check which diagram spaces the three waves evenly by about $120^{\circ}$ or one-third of a wavelength so a peak, a trough and an intermediate value cancel.
walkthrough: The three waves have the same amplitude $a$ and frequency, so at this instant each contributes a displacement between $+a$ and $-a$ depending on its phase.
By the principle of superposition the resultant displacement is the algebraic sum $y = y_1 + y_2 + y_3$ at the same position and time.
Complete cancellation to $y = 0$ needs the phases to be spread evenly around a full $360^{\circ}$ cycle, about $120^{\circ}$ apart, so positive and negative contributions balance.
Only one diagram shows this even spacing with one wave near a peak, one near a trough and one crossing in the opposite sense, giving $y_1 + y_2 + y_3 = 0$.
In the other diagrams two or three waves are close in phase and reinforce to give a large resultant that cannot be cancelled by the remaining wave.

options.A: The three equal waves are spaced by about one-third of a cycle so their instantaneous displacements sum to zero by the principle of superposition.
options.B: Two waves are almost in phase and reinforce while the third cannot cancel their combined displacement.
options.C: All three waves are almost in phase so their displacements add to a large non-zero resultant.
options.D: The three waves are not evenly spread in phase so their instantaneous displacements do not fully cancel.
